secp256k1 ECDSA — decred dcrec pure-Go implementation (provider)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored ethers.js v6.11.0 (adapted for the Ardan blockchain) ships a full @noble/curves secp256k1 implementation in the Chrome wallet extension: ECDSA signing (secp256k1.sign, line 6950), ECDH shared-secret derivation (secp256k1.getSharedSecret, line 6983 — quantum-vulnerable key agreement), public-key derivation, and point arithmetic. All 15 sites are genuine curve constants/operations on one object; keys here sign wallet transactions. Changeable here (vendored copy is first-party-maintained).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardcoded credentials committed in shipped code. The two JS literals are ethers.js's baked-in third-party provider tokens, live in the Chrome extension bundle; the six Go literals are committed secp256k1 key material for the test network.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum keystore (Web3 secret storage v3) wallet encryption in the Chrome extension: scrypt/pbkdf2 derives the key, AES-128-CTR encrypts the private key, a keccak256 MAC authenticates the ciphertext.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared in app/services/viewer/package-lock.json only. node-forge's RSA ships inside the React viewer's dev toolchain: react-scripts → webpack-dev-server → selfsigned@2.0.1 → node-forge@1.3.1, used to generate the dev HTTPS certificate. No application code imports it (viewer package.json has no crypto deps). Dependency inventory entry — present in the shipped node_modules tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The wallet's transaction-signing asset: keys live in .ecdsa files, signatures are ECDSA over secp256k1. Classical signature scheme broken by Shor — a deadline migration item (ML-DSA-65), not a harvest item.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is the Ethereum ecosystem's canonical hash (tx ids, addresses, signing envelopes); on the Go side it produces the Ardan signed-message digest. SHA-3 family — quantum-resistant, kept as a low-urgency asset.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt is the memory-hard KDF protecting encrypted Ethereum keystore wallets in the Chrome extension (Web3 secret storage v3). Symmetric, quantum-robust; parameters come from each keystore JSON.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 protects the extension's wallet files in three formats: Web3 keystore v3 (config-driven PRF), BIP-39 mnemonic seeds, and the obsolete 2014 crowdsale format. Iteration counts (2048/2000) are governed by each format's specification.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is the Go blockchain's workhorse digest: default merkle-tree strategy and the Ardan Hash() used for block/tx ids. On the JS side it is the PBKDF2 PRF for the crowdsale format. Quantum-resistant (Grover only halves preimage cost).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared in app/services/viewer/package-lock.json only, via the same chain react-scripts → webpack-dev-server → selfsigned → node-forge@1.3.1 (dev HTTPS tooling). node-forge's AES is not used by the application itself; it ships with the dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto is the shipped SHA-3/Keccak provider; the reachability is via go-ethereum's crypto.Keccak256 used by the Ardan signature stamp.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHAKE128 is available in the shipped x/crypto/sha3 library but has no direct call site in the application — recorded as a library-surface capability, use is a downstream question.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-512 in the extension bundle: the HMAC-SHA-512 PRF for BIP-39 seed derivation and the sha512 option of the keystore PBKDF2. Largest standard SHA-2 digest — meets CNSA 2.0.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHAKE256 is the CNSA 2.0-recommended XOF and ships in the dependency tree; recorded as available capability with no direct call site in the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 is vendored into the viewer's node_modules via react-scripts → webpack-dev-server → selfsigned → node-forge. It ships RSA, AES, X.509, TLS and PKCS implementations; no first-party call site exists in the viewer app source. Presence is what the inventory records — the dev toolchain relies on it to build the HTTPS dev server cert.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@2.0.1 (declared in the viewer lockfile, required by webpack-dev-server) generates a self-signed certificate for the dev HTTPS server during react-scripts development. Transitive dev dependency, no application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge's X.509 implementation (via selfsigned → webpack-dev-server) is what materializes the viewer's dev HTTPS certificate chain. Transitive dev-toolchain dependency of react-scripts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: "Extended Go cryptography" is the module-level view of the same golang.org/x/crypto@v0.55.0 dependency as LIB-a2c61150: declared in go.mod:27 (indirect via go-ethereum), vendored, sha3 sub-package on the blockchain Keccak-256 hashing path. Same logical asset reached under a different name.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto/rand is the blockchain's randomness source for proof-of-work nonces — OS CSPRNG, the correct choice; kept as the positive control.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto@v0.55.0 is the module dependency of the Ardan blockchain build (go.mod:27, marked indirect — pulled in by go-ethereum). Its sha3 sub-package provides the Keccak-256 that go-ethereum's crypto package uses for the blockchain's block/merkle/signature hashing. Vendored under vendor/golang.org/x/crypto.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The sha3 sub-package of golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 (vendored at vendor/golang.org/x/crypto/sha3) supplies the LegacyKeccak256/Keccak-256 primitive that the vendored go-ethereum crypto package (crypto.Keccak256) builds on — the hash behind the Ardan chain's block headers, merkle roots and signature stamps (foundation/blockchain/signature/signature.go:178). Under the `ziren` build tag that implementation is swapped for the Ziren zkVM Keccak-256 syscall. No first-party file imports x/crypto/sha3 d

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@2.0.1 is the direct cert generator used by webpack-dev-server (react-scripts 5) in app/services/viewer — it mints the self-signed HTTPS certificate for local development and depends on node-forge@1.3.1. No runtime application use; the dependency inventory records its presence and version.
